newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - PARCELLS CAN COACH JETS THIS YEAR AFTER DEAL WITH PATRIOTS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - PARCELLS CAN COACH JETS THIS YEAR AFTER DEAL WITH PATRIOTS.

text.p: Super Bowl coach Bill Parcells can begin coaching the New York Jets immediately after NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue brokered a deal on Monday between the Jets and New England Patriots.

After more than six hours of meetings with Jets owner Leon Hess and Patriots owner Bob Kraft, Tagliabue announced a resolution to the coaching controversy that he declared would make fans of both the Patriots and Jets happy.

The Jets will give up four draft picks over three years to New England for the right to have Parcells on the sidelines for the 1997 season. But they did not have to relinquish this year's number one overall pick, which Kraft had demanded.
The Patriots will receive the Jets' third and fourth round draft picks this year, the second round pick in 1998 and a first round selection in 1999.
Both sides agreed to allow Tagliabue to determine the compensation package after failing to reach an agreement in negotiations.
"The Commissioner did a great job," said Jets owner Leon Hess. "We'll abide by the ruling and are very happy to have Bill Parcells coaching the team."
"I'm not really happy," Kraft said. "But we did this because we thought it was in the best interests of the game."
The Jets, who went a miserable 1-15 last season, also agreed to donate $300,000 to the Patriots' charitable foundation.

Tagliabue convened the hearing Monday morning with Kraft, Parcells' agent Robert Fraley, Hess and Jets president Steve Gutman and urged both sides to reach an agreement "in the best interests of the game."
The commissioner had determined that Parcells' agreement to work with the Jets as a consultant for the 1997 season still required the Patriots' consent or compensation.

But the Jets steadfastly refused to give up the number one pick they earned by losing 15 games and the two sides could not agree on an alternative package of draft choices in exchange for Parcells' coaching services.
Finally, both sides agreed to binding arbitration with Tagliabue to determine the compensation.
Monday's meeting marked the second time Tagliabue had been asked to intervene in the Parcells controversy.
Immediately following the January 26 Super Bowl, the commissioner was asked by Kraft and Parcells to decide whether Parcells' contract with the Patriots allowed him to coach elsewhere next season.
Tagliabue on January 29 sided with the Pats, ruling that Parcells could not serve as an NFL head coach or in a comparable position in 1997 without New England's consent.
But the Jets were determined to land the man who led the New York Giants to two Super Bowl titles and brought respectability to the Patriots.

Last Wednesday they attempted to sidestep the Tagliabue ruling and demands for compensation by naming Parcells a consultant for the 1997 season with the understanding that he would take over the team in 1998.
They named Parcells' long-time right hand man, Bill Belichick, head coach for 1997, with a job as assistant to Parcells beginning in 1998.
Kraft labeled the consultant job "a transparent farce" and formally askeded Tagliabue to step in, leading to Monday's settlement.
Parcells signed a six-year contract with the Jets last Friday.
